rationale: The stock has already dropped roughly 17% from its prior close with no news catalyst, making the move difficult to interpret directionally — it could be a continued flush or a snap-back, but with price sitting only 6.4% off the session low and the 1-minute candles showing tight, low-conviction consolidation near $20.95, there is no clear momentum signal in either direction. The wide bid-ask spread (52.5 bps) and 44 minutes to forced liquidation add friction and time-pressure risk. With today already showing a realized loss and the account near its daily loss budget, the asymmetric risk of being wrong on a volatile, news-free gap-down outweighs any potential edge.
